summary: Yuguang Liu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and completed a PhD at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1964 to 1974. He later served as president (学長) of Taisho University from circa 2010 to 2014.

Yui Chi Lau (1914–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teacher Yingguang Qu. He founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society and taught Shek-wing Tam.

Yui Suzuki works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and the University of Vienna. A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, he held posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and Soka University.

Yuichi Shionoya (1932–2015) was a scholar in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Nagoya University (circa 1950–1953) and Hitotsubashi University (circa 1954–1958), and held an academic post at Nagoya University from circa 1968 to 1974.

Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. Specializing in Buddhist studies, he served as associate professor at Bukkyo University (1961–1997), president of Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (1997), and head of Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen (~1998–2006).

Yujiro Motora (1858–1912) studied at Johns Hopkins University in 1885. Working in philosophy and other fields, he held appointments at the University of Tokyo (circa 1888–1912) and Tokyo University of Education, and taught Daijō Tokiwa.

Yujun Endo (1939–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who taught Kokan Fujita and Ryuichi Abe. He held posts at Taisho University as associate professor (attested 1991) and professor emeritus (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani is a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 2015, she was attested as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Ryukoku University and Hanazono University.

Yukei Matsunaga (1929–2023) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Koyasan, Tohoku, and Kyushu universities, became director at Koyasan University in 1983, and held a post at Shuchiin University.
Yuki Takatsukasa is a Buddhist studies researcher who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015). Takatsukasa later held a position there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He served as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as a Ministry of Education overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

Yukihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981) and under Michael Hahn (attested 1987), later serving as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College.

Yukihisa Yamao (1935–2021) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from circa 1954 to 1963 and subsequently held an academic post there from circa 1968 to 2005.

Yukio Hattori (1932–2007) was a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University from circa 1950 to 1954 and later held an academic post at Japan Women's University from circa 1968 to 1974.

Yukio Kotani (born 1931) studied under Hanjiro Tominaga. Working in Buddhist studies and other fields, he served as professor emeritus of comparative literature at Rissho University from circa 1980 to 2002.

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Daito Shimaji, and Nichien Fukami. A Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Toyo University and served as professor and president at Rissho University.

Yukio Takeda (1934–2021) was an archaeology and history scholar. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1962), he held posts at Nagoya City University (~1968–1973), Hokkaido University (~1973–1977), the University of Tokyo (~1977–1995), and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (~2000–2005).

Yukio Yamanaka is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied as a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and held an appointment as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).
